head_commit.message:
Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CPU implementation of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with C++ kernels in a new `_math` extension, vectorized with Highway and parallelized across threads for large arrays. Both kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`), support sharded execution and `jax.export`, and fix batch partitioning for custom calls when all dimensions are batch dimensions.

display_title: Add common CPU FFI thread pool parallel loop helper and use it in LAPACK kernels.

head_commit.message:
Add common CPU FFI thread pool parallel loop helper and use it in LAPACK kernels.

Adds `jax::FfiThreadPoolAdapter` and `jax::ParallelFor` in `third_party/py/jax/jaxlib/cpu/thread_pool.h` backed by XLA:CPU's work-stealing `Worker::Parallelize`, and updates `ParallelBatchMap` in `third_party/py/jax/jaxlib/cpu/lapack_kernels.cc` to use it instead of scheduling per-chunk heap-allocated tasks via `absl::BlockingCounter`.

Previously, `ParallelBatchMap` queued all chunk tasks onto the XLA:CPU intra-op thread pool and blocked in `absl::BlockingCounter::Wait()`, which could exhaust all pool threads and deadlock when multiple batched LAPACK ops ran concurrently on the pool (the same thread-pool starvation deadlock as https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41265). Switching to `Worker::Parallelize` runs work on the calling thread and uses work stealing to drain queued work without starving the pool.

head_commit.message:
Ensure maybe_recover_user_shardings works as before even when constants are hoisted

Under simplified constants (use_simplified_jaxpr_constants=True), closed-over constants are hoisted and prepended to in_shardings. Because maybe_recover_user_shardings only inspects the first input to recover user NamedSharding (e.g. PartitionSpecs with trailing None), prepending constants caused outputs to be compared against constant shardings instead of user inputs,
resulting in some incorrect results, as shown in the added test.

Slice off hoisted const_args before calling maybe_recover_user_shardings so only actual user arguments are inspected, preserving the exact legacy behavior.

display_title: [consts] Respect LoweringParameters.hoist_constants_as_args in composite and call lowerings

head_commit.message:
[consts] Respect LoweringParameters.hoist_constants_as_args in composite and call lowerings

When exporting or lowering with hoist_constants_as_args=False (as set by
jax.export.export), call_lowering and _composite_lowering were unconditionally
calling core.jaxpr_const_args(call_jaxpr). Because core.jaxpr_const_args only
checks the global config.use_simplified_jaxpr_constants flag, constants
in composite operations (e.g. Fast Walsh Hadamard transformation matrices
in edgetpu.fast_walsh_hadamard_transform and mojax.tag) were hoisted into
dynamic function arguments of the composite op, ignoring
lowering_parameters.hoist_constants_as_args. This creates problems for
projects such as TFLite that do not expected hoisted constants.

Gate core.jaxpr_const_args on lowering_parameters.hoist_constants_as_args in
call_lowering and _composite_lowering so that constants remain statically inlined
during export and whenever hoist_constants_as_args=False is requested.

head_commit.message:
Align MAGMA host complex buffers in hybrid_kernels.cc to GPU complex alignment.

MAGMA typedefs magmaFloatComplex and magmaDoubleComplex to the GPU vendor complex vector types (such as cuFloatComplex and cuDoubleComplex on CUDA), which require 8-byte and 16-byte alignment respectively, whereas std::complex<float> and std::complex<double> only require 4-byte and 8-byte alignment. When operator new[] returns an 8-byte-aligned std::complex<double> buffer, aligned SIMD accesses inside MAGMA's magma_zgeev routines fault with SIGSEGV.

Use the GPU vendor complex types (gpuComplex / gpuDoubleComplex) in EigCompMagma and EigComp's HostBuffer allocations, and align HostBuffer<T> allocations to alignof(T).

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Add F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X{3,4} DotAlgorithmPreset values

Add `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` and `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` to `jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset` and `jax_default_matmul_precision` to expose the StableHLO 1.21.0 3 operation and 4 operation `float8_e4m3fn` dot emulation algorithms for `bfloat16` and `float32` inputs, requiring `jaxlib_extension_version >= 505`.

Each operand is scaled per channel by `2^(-S)`, extracted from the IEEE 754 exponent of its contracting axis maximum magnitude, placing the channel maximum in `[128, 256)`. Rounding the scaled operand to `float8_e4m3fn` forms the high slice (`A_high`, `B_high`) with the top 4 significand bits. Subtracting the high slice in `float32` gives the exact signed residual, which is multiplied by `2^4` and rounded to `float8_e4m3fn` to form the low slice (`A_low`, `B_low`) with the next 4 significand bits.

`F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` sums 3 `float8_e4m3fn` dots from smallest magnitude to largest in `float32`, `(A_low @ B_high + A_high @ B_low) * 2^(-4) + A_high @ B_high`, omitting `A_low @ B_low`. `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` adds `(A_low @ B_low) * 2^(-8)` first as a 4th `float8_e4m3fn` dot, recovering all 8 `bfloat16` significand bits. Multiplying the `float32` sum by `2^(S_A + S_B)` restores the output scale before casting to the result type.

head_commit.message:
Expose the stable Pallas and Pallas TPU APIs as `jax.pallas` and `jax.pallas.tpu`.

Users can now write `from jax import pallas as pl` and `from jax.pallas import tpu as pltpu`. Like `jax.extend`, `jax.pallas` is a subpackage that is not imported by `import jax`. The implementation stays in `jax._src.pallas`.

The new modules export the stable API surface centered around `pl.kernel` and `pltpu.emit_pipeline`. The following APIs stay only in `jax.experimental.pallas` / `jax.experimental.pallas.tpu` for now:

* `pallas_call` and the APIs only used with it: `pl.pallas_call`, `pl.GridSpec`, `pl.RevisitMode`, `pltpu.PrefetchScalarGridSpec`, `pltpu.CORE_PARALLEL`, `pltpu.SUBCORE_PARALLEL` and `pltpu.with_memory_space_constraint`.
* APIs that are still experimental or are too specialized to become public: `pl.pallas_call_p`, `pl.lower_as_mlir`, `pl.pallas_export_experimental`, `pl.get_global`, `pl.dslice` (use `pl.ds`), the Triton-only `pl.next_power_of_2`, `pl.strides_from_shape` and `pl.broadcast_to`, `pltpu.reciprocal`, and the internal `pltpu.core` module.
* APIs with no users outside of JAX: `pl.enable_poison_buffers`, `pl.semaphore`, `pl.squeezed` (use `pl.Squeezed()` or `None`), `pltpu.CMEM`, `pltpu.CoreType`, `pltpu.LoweringException`, `pltpu.conv`, `pltpu.dma_semaphore`, `pltpu.emit_pipeline_with_async_prefetch`, `pltpu.has_memory_space`, `pltpu.join_bits`, `pltpu.split_bits`, `pltpu.pack_fp6`, `pltpu.unpack_fp6`, `pltpu.load`, `pltpu.matmul_acc_lhs`, `pltpu.matmul_lhs_fifo`, `pltpu.matmul_pop_fifo`, `pltpu.stateful_bernoulli`, `pltpu.stateful_bits` and `pltpu.stateful_normal`.
* Deprecated aliases (`pl.core_map`, `pl.DeviceIdType`, `pl.reciprocal`, `pltpu.BufferedRefBase`, `pltpu.create_tensorcore_mesh`) are not carried over.

`jax.experimental.pallas` and `jax.experimental.pallas.tpu` re-export `jax.pallas` and `jax.pallas.tpu`, and also keep exporting the APIs above with their existing deprecations, so existing imports keep working unchanged. The other backend modules (`tpu_sc`, `mosaic_gpu`, `triton`, `fuser`) and `jax.experimental.pallas.ops` are unchanged.

`tests/pallas/tpu_pallas_test.py` now imports `jax.pallas` and `jax.pallas.tpu`, and uses `jax.experimental.pallas[.tpu]` only for the APIs listed above.

display_title: Fix value-level set_xla_metadata() when an op's output is wrapped in sdy.sharding_constraint.

head_commit.message:
Fix value-level set_xla_metadata() when an op's output is wrapped in sdy.sharding_constraint.

On meshes with mixed or explicit sharding (e.g. shard_map with both manual and
auto axes), ops such as `fori_loop` emit two MLIR ops and return the second:
```
   %w = stablehlo.while(...)
   %s = sdy.sharding_constraint %w <sharding>
```

This causes `set_xla_metadata(out, ...)` to attach metadata to the sharding
constraint (`%s`) instead of the underlying op (`%w`), and Shardy to later drop `%s`
during partitioning.

In this change, we fix the logic so that `set_xla_metadata()` is applied to the right operation.

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Fix jax.scipy.special.betaln for negative integers, zero, and infinite inputs (jax-ml/jax#38243, jax-ml/jax#39106)

Problem:
1. In jax-ml/jax#38243 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38243), `jax.scipy.special.betaln(a, b)` returns `NaN` when one argument is a negative integer `-n` and the other is a positive integer `b <= n`, because `lax.lgamma(new_a)` and `lax.lgamma(new_a + new_b)` both evaluate to `inf` at non-positive integer poles and cancel as `inf - inf`. In addition, when `new_a < 0` and `new_b >= 8` without integer reflection such that `new_a + new_b < 8`, `betaln` routed to `algdiv`, where `a / b <= -1` yields `NaN` in `lax.log1p(a / b)` or inaccurate Stirling series values, and `algdiv` had a pre-existing `x = h / (1 + h)` typo instead of `x = 1.0 / (1.0 + h)`.
2. In jax-ml/jax#39106 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39106), `jax.scipy.special.betaln` returns `NaN` on infinite and zero boundary arguments (and fails under `jax.debug_nans(True)`):
   - In `algdiv(a, b)`, when `b` is infinite, `u = d * lax.log1p(a / b)` evaluates `inf * 0 = NaN` and `v = a * (lax.log(b) - 1.0)` evaluates `0 * inf = NaN` when `a == 0`.
   - In `betaln(a, b)`, because `jnp.where` evaluates both branches, the unselected `small_b` branch evaluates `lgamma(inf) - lgamma(a + inf) = inf - inf = NaN` when `b = inf` (and `lgamma(b) - lgamma(a + b) = inf - inf = NaN` when both `a` and `b` are non-positive integers), while the unselected `large_b` branch evaluates `algdiv(0, 0)` (`0 / 0 = NaN`) when `b < 8`.

Solution:
1. Apply the beta reflection identity `betaln(a, b) = betaln(1 - a - b, b)` when `new_a` is a finite negative integer, `new_b` is a finite positive integer, and `new_a <= -new_b` (checking integrality via `lax.rem`), then re-sort the reflected pair when `reflect & (new_a > new_b)` so `new_a <= new_b` holds and gradients at `reflected_a == new_b` remain consistent.
2. Route both `new_b < 8` and `new_a + new_b < 8` (`(new_b < 8) | (new_a < 8 - new_b)`) to `small_b`, and fix `x = 1.0 / (1.0 + h)` in `algdiv` per `cdflib/algdiv.f`.
3. In `algdiv`, replace `u` with its asymptotic limit `a` when `b` is infinite (masking `d_safe = jnp.where(b_is_inf, 0.0, d)` in the false branch) and guard `v` when `b_is_inf & (a == 0.0)` (masking `a_safe = jnp.where(b_is_inf & (a == 0.0), 1.0, a)` in the false branch so gradients at `a = 0` are preserved for finite `b`).
4. In `betaln`, mask the inputs to `(lgamma(b) - lgamma(a + b))` in `small_b` unless `is_small_b & ~(is_nonpos_int_a & is_nonpos_int_b)` and mask the inputs to `algdiv` in `large_b` when `is_small_b`, avoiding unselected `NaN`s under `jax.debug_nans(True)` and returning `+inf` when both inputs are non-positive integers or one is `0.0`.
5. Add regression tests `testBetalnNegativeIntegers` and `testBetalnInf` in `lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38243
Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39106

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Add F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X{3,4} DotAlgorithmPreset values

Add `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` and `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` to `jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset` and `jax_default_matmul_precision` to expose the StableHLO 1.21.0 3 operation and 4 operation `float8_e4m3fn` dot emulation algorithms for `bfloat16` and `float32` inputs, requiring `jaxlib_extension_version >= 505`.

Each operand is scaled per channel by `2^(-S)`, extracted from the IEEE 754 exponent of its contracting axis maximum magnitude, placing the channel maximum in `[128, 256)`. Rounding the scaled operand to `float8_e4m3fn` forms the high slice (`A_high`, `B_high`) with the top 4 significand bits. Subtracting the high slice in `float32` gives the exact signed residual, which is multiplied by `2^4` and rounded to `float8_e4m3fn` to form the low slice (`A_low`, `B_low`) with the next 4 significand bits.

`F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` sums 3 `float8_e4m3fn` dots from smallest magnitude to largest in `float32`, `(A_low @ B_high + A_high @ B_low) * 2^(-4) + A_high @ B_high`, omitting `A_low @ B_low`. `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` adds `(A_low @ B_low) * 2^(-8)` first as a 4th `float8_e4m3fn` dot, recovering all 8 `bfloat16` significand bits. Multiplying the `float32` sum by `2^(S_A + S_B)` restores the output scale before casting to the result type.

display_title: Set lax.lgamma accuracy to 1 ULP across CPU, GPU, and TPU, and stop using late inlining for lgamma/digamma on GPU.

head_commit.message:
Set lax.lgamma accuracy to 1 ULP across CPU, GPU, and TPU, and stop using late inlining for lgamma/digamma on GPU.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` reached up to 4 ULP error in `float32` on GPU and TPU and up to 2 ULP error in `float64` due to rounding in leading logarithm and polynomial terms and cancellation in Euler's reflection formula near negative zeros. In addition, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` used `Inline.XLA_LATE` on GPU, which XLA:GPU does not inline, leaving every op inside wrapped in its own single-op kernel.

Switch `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` to `inline=False` on GPU (keeping `Inline.XLA_LATE` on CPU only) so XLA:GPU inlines and fuses them normally, and add `split_bits` in `double_word.py` for bitmask significand splitting across `float32` and `float64`.

On GPU and TPU in `float32`, split the leading logarithm, Stirling, and reflection terms into `(hi, lo)` pairs (reducing the remaining polynomial degrees) and replace the `(delta - r) / (delta + r)` polynomials near negative zeros with degree-11 polynomials in `(delta - r) * scale` that avoid division (including a separate branch around the local minimum on `(-3, -2)`), trading extra HLO instructions for 1 ULP accuracy. In `float64`, use the same `(delta - r) * scale` form at degree 15 instead of degree 20 and lower the Stirling shift threshold from 8 to 7, reducing `float64` HLO size while reaching 1 ULP.

On CPU, simplify the `float32` path (which promotes to `float64`) by shifting arguments below 8 up to at least 8 for Stirling's series with `lax.log` and using short Taylor polynomials near 1 and 2, cutting CPU `float32` HLO size by 43-44% while staying within 1.0 ULP without point overrides. Update `accuracy.md` and `gamma_test` to use a uniform 1.0 ULP `lgamma` bound across CPU, GPU, and TPU in `float32` and `float64` (relaxing CPU `float32` from 0.5 to 1.0 ULP so the bound does not depend on platform `libm` or FMA rounding near `float32` midpoint ties).

Pre-optimization StableHLO op counts for `lax.lgamma` (`lowered.as_text()`, `old -> new`):

| Backend | Dtype | 1D array | Scalar |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CPU | `float32` | 461 -> 309 (-152, -33%) | 344 -> 241 (-103, -30%) |
| CPU | `float64` | 985 -> 945 (-40, -4%) | 829 -> 789 (-40, -5%) |
| GPU | `float32` | 466 -> 539 (+73, +16%) | 370 -> 442 (+72, +19%) |
| GPU | `float64` | 985 -> 945 (-40, -4%) | 829 -> 789 (-40, -5%) |
| TPU | `float32` | 466 -> 539 (+73, +16%) | 370 -> 442 (+72, +19%) |

Post-optimization HLO instruction counts for `lax.lgamma` (`lowered.compile().as_text()`, `old -> new`):

| Backend | Dtype | 1D array | Scalar |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CPU | `float32` | 494 -> 279 (-215, -44%) | 386 -> 219 (-167, -43%) |
| CPU | `float64` | 1,447 -> 1,286 (-161, -11%) | 1,265 -> 1,123 (-142, -11%) |
| GPU (H100) | `float32` | 1,463 -> 596 (-867, -59%) | 1,240 -> 510 (-730, -59%) |
| GPU (H100) | `float64` | 3,826 -> 1,261 (-2,565, -67%) | 3,446 -> 1,310 (-2,136, -62%) |
| TPU | `float32` | 1,075 -> 1,382 (+307, +29%) | 423 -> 507 (+84, +20%) |

display_title: Set lax.lgamma accuracy to 1 ULP across CPU, GPU, and TPU, and stop using late inlining for lgamma/digamma on GPU.

head_commit.message:
Set lax.lgamma accuracy to 1 ULP across CPU, GPU, and TPU, and stop using late inlining for lgamma/digamma on GPU.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` reached up to 4 ULP error in `float32` on GPU and TPU and up to 2 ULP error in `float64` due to rounding in leading logarithm and polynomial terms and cancellation in Euler's reflection formula near negative zeros. In addition, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` used `Inline.XLA_LATE` on GPU, which XLA:GPU does not inline, leaving every op inside wrapped in its own single-op kernel.

Switch `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` to `inline=False` on GPU (keeping `Inline.XLA_LATE` on CPU only) so XLA:GPU inlines and fuses them normally, and add `split_bits` in `double_word.py` for bitmask significand splitting across `float32` and `float64`.

On GPU and TPU in `float32`, split the leading logarithm, Stirling, and reflection terms into `(hi, lo)` pairs (reducing the remaining polynomial degrees) and replace the `(delta - r) / (delta + r)` polynomials near negative zeros with degree-11 polynomials in `(delta - r) * scale` that avoid division (including a separate branch around the local minimum on `(-3, -2)`), trading extra HLO instructions for 1 ULP accuracy. In `float64`, use the same `(delta - r) * scale` form at degree 15 instead of degree 20 and lower the Stirling shift threshold from 8 to 7, reducing `float64` HLO size while reaching 1 ULP.

On CPU, simplify the `float32` path (which promotes to `float64`) by shifting arguments below 8 up to at least 8 for Stirling's series with `lax.log` and using short Taylor polynomials near 1 and 2, cutting CPU `float32` HLO size by 43-44% while staying within 1.0 ULP without point overrides. Update `accuracy.md` and `gamma_test` to use a uniform 1.0 ULP `lgamma` bound across CPU, GPU, and TPU in `float32` and `float64` (relaxing CPU `float32` from 0.5 to 1.0 ULP so the bound does not depend on platform `libm` or FMA rounding near `float32` midpoint ties).

Pre-optimization StableHLO op counts for `lax.lgamma` (`lowered.as_text()`, `old -> new`):

| Backend | Dtype | 1D array | Scalar |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CPU | `float32` | 461 -> 309 (-152, -33%) | 344 -> 241 (-103, -30%) |
| CPU | `float64` | 985 -> 945 (-40, -4%) | 829 -> 789 (-40, -5%) |
| GPU | `float32` | 466 -> 539 (+73, +16%) | 370 -> 442 (+72, +19%) |
| GPU | `float64` | 985 -> 945 (-40, -4%) | 829 -> 789 (-40, -5%) |
| TPU | `float32` | 466 -> 539 (+73, +16%) | 370 -> 442 (+72, +19%) |

Post-optimization HLO instruction counts for `lax.lgamma` (`lowered.compile().as_text()`, `old -> new`):

| Backend | Dtype | 1D array | Scalar |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CPU | `float32` | 494 -> 279 (-215, -44%) | 386 -> 219 (-167, -43%) |
| CPU | `float64` | 1,447 -> 1,286 (-161, -11%) | 1,265 -> 1,123 (-142, -11%) |
| GPU (H100) | `float32` | 1,463 -> 596 (-867, -59%) | 1,240 -> 510 (-730, -59%) |
| GPU (H100) | `float64` | 3,826 -> 1,261 (-2,565, -67%) | 3,446 -> 1,310 (-2,136, -62%) |
| TPU | `float32` | 1,075 -> 1,382 (+307, +29%) | 423 -> 507 (+84, +20%) |

With `inline=False` on both sides on GPU (isolating the `lgamma` changes from the inlining fix), post-optimization GPU `float32` is 518 -> 596 (+78, +15%) for 1D and 410 -> 510 (+100, +24%) for scalar, and GPU `float64` is 1,258 -> 1,261 (+3, +0%) for 1D and 1,216 -> 1,310 (+94, +8%) for scalar.

display_title: Preserve operand layout in reshape transpose and format aval layouts.

head_commit.message:
Preserve operand layout in reshape transpose and format aval layouts.

Under `explicit_layout`, `reshape` places per-shard size-1 dimensions at the major-most positions always. When an operand to `reshape` has size-1 shard dimension in a non-majormost but still major slot (such as from PJRT's default layout or after `transpose` or `split`), transposing `reshape` reconstructs the cotangent with that singleton dimension moved to slot 0, failing the layout check in `typematch` even though both layouts describe the same physical buffer.

Apply `pjit.relayout` in `_reshape_transpose_rule` when the reshaped cotangent layout differs from `operand.aval.layout` so the metadata-only singleton ordering matches without data movement. We can consider adding `out_layout` to reshape in future.

Also include concrete `Layout` metadata (`L(...)`, optional `T(...)`, and optional `E(...)`) in `ShapedArray` short string formatting so layout mismatches are visible in error messages.

[JAX] Fix jax.scipy.special.expi(+inf) returning NaN (jax-ml/jax#38519)

Problem:
In jax-ml/jax#38519 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38519), `jax.scipy.special.expi(np.inf)` returns `NaN` instead of `inf` because `_expi_pos` has no condition for `+inf` and falls through to `_expint7`, which evaluates `exp(inf) * (1 / inf)`. Solution:
Add an explicit `jnp.isposinf(x)` condition returning `np.inf` in `_expi_pos`, sanitize out-of-domain inputs in `_expint1`, `_eval_expint_k`, and `_expi_neg` for `jax.debug_nans(True)` safety, and add a regression test `testExpiInf` in `lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38519

head_commit.message:
[pallas] Raise when an mpmd_map (pl.kernel) kernel writes to an immutable array input.

`mpmd_map` (and so `pl.kernel`) passes every input to the kernel as a Ref, but only discharges writes into operand-output aliasing for inputs that are Refs at the call site. Writes to plain array inputs were silently dropped from the effects, so the kernel mutated an HLO operand that XLA treats as read-only.

Raise a `ValueError` instead, pointing at the input and suggesting `jax.new_ref` or `out_type`.

`MpmdTest.test_vmap` called `pltpu.touch`, which declares a write, on an array input; pass it a Ref instead.

Several GPU interpret mode tests pass a plain array to `plgpu.kernel`, so wrap these in `jax.new_ref`.

display_title: Add common CPU FFI thread pool parallel loop helper and use it in LAPACK kernels.

head_commit.message:
Add common CPU FFI thread pool parallel loop helper and use it in LAPACK kernels.

Adds `jax::FfiThreadPoolAdapter` and `jax::ParallelFor` in `third_party/py/jax/jaxlib/cpu/thread_pool.h` backed by XLA:CPU's work-stealing `Worker::Parallelize`, and updates `ParallelBatchMap` in `third_party/py/jax/jaxlib/cpu/lapack_kernels.cc` to use it instead of scheduling per-chunk heap-allocated tasks via `absl::BlockingCounter`.

Previously, `ParallelBatchMap` queued all chunk tasks onto the XLA:CPU intra-op thread pool and blocked in `absl::BlockingCounter::Wait()`, which could exhaust all pool threads and deadlock when multiple batched LAPACK ops ran concurrently on the pool (the same thread-pool starvation deadlock as https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41265). Switching to `Worker::Parallelize` runs work on the calling thread and uses work stealing to drain queued work without starving the pool.

head_commit.message:
Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CPU implementation of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with C++ kernels in a new `_math` extension, vectorized with Highway and parallelized across threads for large arrays. Both kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`), support sharded execution and `jax.export`, and fix batch partitioning for custom calls when all dimensions are batch dimensions.
